history.plan: clear carry-over: fix the 041122 page-7 welded cell inset (first line's x -> block's leftmost line x), measure with an empty render dir

context: The carry-over was measured and its premise is false; the engine fix it asked for would have compressed every line of the verification cell. 041122's cell baselines are 12.000 pt apart in the source and the writer already emits w:line=240 tw for them; the row's declared 4630 tw (231.5 pt) and its content (232 pt) agree to 0.5 pt. The '11.6 pt pitch' was 4630 divided by the RENDERED line count. Two things then changed the picture. (1) This slot cloned at 9f7a094 and origin had moved to cf2f9c6, whose ARIAL_W change (runs written in Arial at the character scale that reproduces the page's own advance widths, folio anchored) had already cured the wrap: on the fixed engine 041122 renders 11 pages and item 22b lands on page 7, the page the source drew it on. (2) This slot's own first commit, built from the stale file, silently REVERTED that engine fix; it was caught by diffing against origin and restored (DocxWriter.java is now cf2f9c6 + the probe only). step.py now fetches origin/main and fast-forwards before the slot reads anything, which is the guard against that whole class of loss. What is left on 041122 is two folio-only sheets - our page 8 holds the text '7' alone and our page 10 holds '8' alone - because the folio anchor only fires for a folio in the bottom band and these two are placed where the flow had no room. HYPOTHESES.md carries both corrections at the end; read them before touching the writer.
